name: Translator & Interpreter
title: Translator and Interpreter
intro: The translation roadmap: language training, degrees, certifications, specialisation and career paths.

phases.title: School years: build strong languages
phases.summary: Learn your mother tongue, English and one more language well.
points: Choose languages as subjects and read widely in each.
Start a foreign language such as French, German, Japanese, Spanish, Chinese or Russian through school or online.
Practise writing and speaking regularly.
Learn to translate short texts between your languages for practice.

phases.title: Degree and admission
phases.summary: BA in a language through CUET-UG or merit.
points: Choose BA (Hons) in a language such as English, Hindi, French, German or Japanese.
Central universities use CUET-UG; JNU, DU, EFLU and others offer language programmes.
Select a course with translation and linguistics modules.
Add foreign-language certificate courses alongside the degree.

phases.title: Language levels and certifications
phases.summary: Prove your level with international frameworks.
points: Foreign languages are graded on the CEFR scale A1 to C2; common exams include DELF/DALF (French), Goethe-Zertifikat (German), JLPT (Japanese) and HSK (Chinese).
Aim for at least B2 or C1 level for professional work.
Study translation theory, terminology and editing.
Practise with real documents in specialised domains.

phases.title: Specialise and train
points: Translators work with written texts; interpreters work in real time (consecutive and simultaneous).
Take PG diplomas or master’s in translation studies and interpreting where available.
Specialise in legal, medical, technical, literary or localisation work.
Learn CAT tools such as Trados and memoQ.

phases.title: Careers and job entry
points: Government: Central Translation Bureau, ministries’ Hindi/translation cells and the Staff Selection Commission’s Junior Translator exam.
Private: translation agencies, localisation companies, MNC language support and publishing.
International: UN and other bodies hire through competitive exams.
Freelancing platforms and conference interpretation offer additional routes.
